answer: Opal-filing stops fake farms: one unique opal per identity at a vertex of the public registry. Each opal bears a unique natural plume; the owner photographs it, key-signs the hash, and files it. Auditors match filings against all prior hashes; a rented plume burns the 70-credit bond. First opal 38, thousandth 5,033: 1,000 fakes cost 2,535,500 plus 70,000 locked bonds for a 40,000 pool. Honest agents pay 38 once, keep the bond.
